Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office” or similar) is invalid for these requests; do not select it.
- Valid choices observed are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk).
- Route explicitly urgent or repeatedly followed-up requests to B: “asking twice already,” “second attempt,” or “before end of day.”
- “No rush” and routine wording (“same as last month,” “confirm receipt”) suggest A.
- Large requests may warrant B when urgency or impact is also indicated; size alone has not been validated as sufficient.
- Region (north, south, east), request type (refund, shipment, claim), sender department, and regional-office wording do not establish a separate routing option.

Routing notes:
- Options A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and C (regional office) can all be valid; the earlier rule that C is always invalid is contradicted by recent outcomes.
- A is supported for routine, low-impact requests: “No rush, but please confirm receipt” (refunds) and possibly similar standard cases.
- B is supported by at least one “Second attempt, the first form bounced” invoice, but this is not universally sufficient: the same wording on a shipment was rejected with B.
- Urgency alone is not reliably mapped to B: “before end of day” was rejected with B.
- “Came in through the regional office” does not itself determine routing: accepted as A for refunds, but A was rejected for a north-region claim.
- “Paperwork was scanned, not typed” is a special-case signal; A was rejected for both a claim and a large invoice.
- Request type and contextual combinations matter. Claims (especially north-region claims), scanned paperwork, and some shipment/invoice cases may require C or another nonstandard route. Exact C outcomes are not yet observed, so do not assert a deterministic mapping.
- Region, sender department, and request size alone remain insufficient. Treat urgency, prior attempts, intake channel, paperwork format, request type, and their combinations as routing signals; use confirmed examples cautiously.

Routing notes:
- A, B, and C can all be valid; no option is universally correct.
- A is supported for some routine/low-impact cases, including prior refund examples, but was rejected for: north refund (small, second attempt), south refund (large, urgent), and east shipment (small, urgent).
- B is not reliably triggered by urgency or prior attempts. It was rejected for a south refund (large, repeated client inquiries), an urgent refund, and a shipment where the first form bounced. Treat B as weakly supported only by the earlier accepted invoice example.
- C now has confirmed valid and invalid cases. Accepted: large north-region refund with “same as last month,” and small south-region claim with urgent wording. Rejected: large north-region claim with the same “last month” wording; north-region shipments (large/small, including prior-attempt wording); and earlier cases where C had not been confirmed.
- Region alone is insufficient: north supports C for one refund but not a claim or shipments; south supports C for one claim but not a refund.
- Request type, size, region, urgency, prior attempts, intake channel, sender department, and paperwork format interact. Claims and some refunds may require C; shipments in observed north/east cases did not accept the tested option. Do not generalize from wording alone.
- “Paperwork was scanned, not typed” remains a special-case signal: A was rejected for both a claim and a large invoice; route remains unresolved.
- Use confirmed examples cautiously and avoid asserting deterministic mappings where no matching outcome exists.

Routing notes:
- No universal mapping; request type, size, region, urgency, wording, prior attempts, intake channel, sender department, and paperwork format interact.
- A is valid in some routine/low-impact cases and is now confirmed for a small north shipment with “same as last month.” It was rejected for north small refunds (including regional-office intake), north small claim, north/east shipment cases, and some refund/invoice examples. Do not infer A from routine wording.
- B is weakly supported, not simply triggered by urgency or repeat attempts. Confirmed valid for a large east invoice marked urgent. It was rejected in some south refunds and other prior-attempt/urgent cases.
- C is valid in selected claims/refunds: large north refund with “same as last month,” small south claim urgent, large south claim urgent, and large south claim with scanned paperwork. It is invalid for a large north claim with “last month,” small east urgent claim, north shipments observed previously, and some unconfirmed earlier cases.
- Region alone is insufficient: north has mixed refund/claim/shipment outcomes; south has both valid C claims and invalid C refund examples; east now has a valid B invoice and invalid C claim.
- “Paperwork was scanned, not typed” is no longer wholly unresolved: C is confirmed for the large south claim, but prior scanned claim/invoice cases rejected A do not establish a universal route.
- Options outside A/B/C (e.g., D) are invalid; do not treat their rejection as evidence about the valid options.
- Use exact matching confirmed examples cautiously. Avoid generalizing from urgency, “same as last month,” regional-office intake, sender department, or repeated inquiries alone.

Routing notes:
- No universal mapping; request type, size, region, wording, urgency, prior attempts, intake channel, sender department, and paperwork format interact.
- A is valid only in select routine cases: confirmed for a small north shipment marked “same as last month.” Rejected for north small refunds (including regional-office intake), north small claim, north/east shipment cases, some refund/invoice cases, and a small south invoice. Do not infer A from routine wording.
- B is weakly supported and not triggered reliably by urgency, repeat attempts, or invoice type. Confirmed for one large east invoice marked urgent; rejected for a small north invoice, large north shipment, another large east invoice (“same as last month”), some south refunds, and other urgent/prior-attempt cases.
- C is valid in selected cases: small and large south claims (including non-urgent, urgent, and scanned-paperwork examples), and a large east refund. It is rejected for large east claims (both “same as last month” and repeat-inquiry wording), small east urgent claim, small north claim, large north claim with “last month,” north shipments, and some unconfirmed earlier cases.
- Region alone is insufficient: south has valid C claims but invalid C refunds; east has a valid C refund, a valid B invoice example, and invalid C claims/invoice; north remains mixed.
- Scanned paperwork confirms C for the large south claim only; it does not establish a universal route.
- Options outside A/B/C (e.g., D) are invalid; their rejection says nothing about A/B/C.
- Use exact confirmed matches cautiously. Do not generalize from urgency, “same as last month,” routine wording, regional-office intake, sender department, or repeated inquiries alone.

Routing notes:
- No universal mapping. Request type, size, region, wording, urgency, prior attempts, intake channel, sender department, and paperwork format interact.
- A is valid only in selected cases: confirmed small north shipment (“same as last month”), small north invoice with scanned paperwork, and small east invoice after repeated inquiry. Rejected for north/south/east refunds in observed cases, north/small claims, north/east shipment cases, some invoice cases, and a small south invoice. Do not infer A from routine wording, repeated attempts, or scanned paperwork alone.
- B remains weak and unreliable. Confirmed for one large east invoice marked urgent; rejected for small north invoice, large north shipment, multiple east invoices (including regional-office intake), south refunds, and other urgent/prior-attempt cases.
- C is valid in selected cases: small and large south claims (urgent, non-urgent, and scanned-paperwork examples) and a large east refund. Rejected for south refunds, east claims/shipments/invoice cases, north claims/shipments, and other unconfirmed cases.
- Region alone is insufficient: south has valid C claims but observed refunds reject A/B; east has a valid C refund and isolated A invoice, while B/C fail in other east cases; north remains mixed.
- Scanned paperwork does not imply C; it coincided with accepted A for a small north invoice and previously confirmed C for a large south claim.
- “Same as last month,” urgency, regional-office intake, sender department, routine wording, and repeated inquiries are not reliable routing rules.
- Options outside A/B/C (e.g., D) are invalid; rejecting them says nothing about the remaining options.
- Use exact confirmed matches cautiously; when no close confirmed match exists, avoid pattern-based guessing.
